adapter.name: eventkg
adapter.license: UNRESOLVED for the biography half -- see experiments/corpora/eventkg/README.md; Wikipedia abstracts are CC BY-SA 4.0
adapter.metric: recall of Wikipedia-attested temporal relations per person, name-anchored (weak) and date-anchored (strong); no precision -- see module docstring

repeats.metric: recall of Wikipedia-attested temporal relations per person, name-anchored (weak) and date-anchored (strong); no precision -- see module docstring

not_applicable.relation_type: gold properties span Wikidata, DBpedia and YAGO, and a large share of rows are `wikipedia:link`, which carries no relation type at all
not_applicable.event_type: no gold row carries an event type
not_applicable.precision: the 0.0 rows are relations EventKG holds but the abstract does not state; an extraction matching one is not demonstrably wrong. Reported as distractor_hit_rate instead
not_applicable.biography_half: `biography_score` was derived from Thefamouspeople.com and Biography.com texts, which the benchmark does not redistribute; those documents cannot be scored

notes: Recall only. The gold's 0.0 rows are unstated-in-abstract, not false, so no precision is computable; distractor_hit_rate reports the rate at which extractions land on them.
Gold is deduplicated on (connected entity, interval): the release labels `actedIn`, `starring` and `P161` separately for one fact.
Date agreement is computed only where the interval is the relation's own validity. 750 name-matched facts carried an interval belonging to the connected entity instead and were excluded from it.
10 gold facts have no English label and cannot be matched by name; one such row carries a birth date.
Abstracts are pinned to the last revision before 2019-05-21, so the text is the text the judgements were made against.

Documents were ordered by scored gold fact count, most first. A run that did not reach the end therefore covers the most-documented people, and its recall is NOT a corpus estimate: report it as recall over the N people with the most attested relations.
The published SVM figures measure relation selection over graph features, with the graph as input and no biography read. They are not a baseline for this task and are omitted from published_baseline.
